name: Dioula d'Odienné, parler de Samatiguila
catalog_citation: Braconnier, Cassian. 1990. Le "morphème tonal d'énoncé incomplet" du dioula d'Odienné. Mandenkan 20: 3-25. (the Internet Archive id_ copy of the LLACAN open Mandenkan archive, https://web.archive.org/web/20140819180044id_/http://llacan.vjf.cnrs.fr/PDF/Mandenk…
catalog_locator: printed p. 4 (and p. 5), section I 'PROPRIETES TONALES', 1.1 'Caractère polaire et flottant de INC' and 1.2.1 'INC et l'expansion de ton haut vers la gauche'; …
catalog_quote: INC prend une valeur tonale inverse de celle du ton auquel il fait suite. Le dioula d'Odienné est une langue à deux tons phonologiques (voir Braconnier (1983a et b): INC sera donc formé d'un ton haut après ton bas et d'un ton bas après ton haut. C'est ce que nous exprimons en disant que INC est un morphème "à polarité tonale". Après attachement de INC à la voyelle qui précède, cette voyelle se trouve toujours réalisée avec un schème tonal modulé, bas-haut ou haut-bas, selon la nature du ton propre de ladite voyelle, comme l'illustrent les exemples suivants (où la réalisation phonétique observée est représentée entre crochets). ... [p. 5] 1.2.1 INC et l'expansion de ton haut vers la gauche. Il se trouve qu'en DO existe aussi un processus d'expansion de ton haut vers la gauche. Ce processus a notamment pour effet qu'un ton haut phonologique s'étend sur la surface entière de toute voyelle …

new_statements.translation: INC takes a tonal value opposite to that of the tone it follows. Odienné Dioula is a language with two phonological tones (see Braconnier 1983a and b): INC will therefore consist of a high tone after a low tone and a low tone after a high tone. This is what we express by saying that INC is a morpheme 'with tonal polarity'. After INC attaches to the preceding vowel, that vowel is always realised with a contour tonal scheme, low-high or high-low, according to the vowel's own tone

new_statements.rule_in_words: Odienné Jula is a two-tone (H/L) lexical tone language; the describer of record (Braconnier) states no word-stress rule in any of his openly available papers. The only accentual discussion (Bamba 1990, reanalysing Braconnier 1982-83) treats 'accent' as a metrical reinterpretation of lexical H tone (H = [s w] foot, L = unaccented), with the definite-noun marker realised as a superhigh/lengthened accent on the noun's final syllable; accent location is thus lexical/morphological, not a positional word-stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: Bamba 1990 p.13 (verbatim): 'In Odyene Dyula, it is not easy to distinguish H tone from accent. The only non-problematic identification of an accented position is the definite form of monosyllabic nouns with underlying L. Braconnier (1982: 78, 81, exx. 71, 77) has note[d] a lengthening and accentuation of the definite form of monosyllabic nouns jì "water" and bà "river".' and p.9: 'Trisyllabic nouns show that the accent is limited to the final syllable of the noun'. Braconnier 1990 also describes downdrift and a leftward H-spreading / H-detachment, all tonal.
new_statements.domain_note: Braconnier's statement is about the lexical/phonological tone inventory of the language; Bamba's 'accent' concerns definite noun forms (noun + tonal definite morpheme) and sentence-level downdrift, i.e. morphological/phrasal, not citation-form word stress. Variety: parler de Samatiguila, given by Braconnier as representative of dioula d'Odienné.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe 'le dioula d'Odienné', specifically the parler de Samatiguila (c. 40 km NW of Odienné), which Derive 1985 (Mandenkan 10, p.65 n.1) calls 'wojenekan' and attributes to Braconnier — i.e. Glottolog woje1238 Wojenaka / ISO jod (Odienné Jula), not Burkina/vehicular Dyula (dyul1238). Note the catalog's dyul1238 record already cites Bamba 1990 on this Odienné variety as corroboration; that material properly belongs to woje1238. The Odienné-area varieties show 'tonal inversion' (lexical H where other Manding has L and vice versa).

sources.note: p.1 'The underlying tones are L (low) and H (high)'; metrical reanalysis: lexical H = [s w] foot, L = absence of accent; p.13 'In Odyene Dyula, it is not easy to distinguish H tone from accent. The only non-problematic identification of an accented position is the definite form of monosyllabic nouns with underlying L' (lengthening per Braconnier 1982:78,81); definite accent (superhigh) 'limited to the final syllable of the noun'; conclusion: 'a metrical analysis of a tone language'.
